summary: Iter95 — notification action buttons (Goedkeuren/Afwijzen). Backend: all 20 pytest cases pass (100%). Verified regression on existing /payments/{pid}/approve + /reject, _with_action_token scoping (approval kinds+payment_id+uid only), POST /api/push/action full matrix (approve w/ and w/o saved signature → '(via melding)' suffix + approved_via='notification' persisted in Mongo + signature taken from PUT /me/approval-signature; reject → rejected_reason='Afgewezen via melding'; second use → 409; tampered/expired token → 401; unknown action → 422; non-admin uid → 403), /me/approval-signature GET/PUT roundtrip + invalid 422, /push/fcm/register accepts capabilities=['actions'] and GET /push/fcm/devices does not leak `token` or `capabilities`, and fcm_service._send_one(data_only=True) omits `notification{}` block while data_only=False includes it. sw.js push handler + notificationclick code reviewed — correct (actions only when action_token present; event.action approve/reject → fetch /api/push/action with the signed token). Frontend: headless Chromium repeatedly crashes (Target crashed) when loading /{slug}/admin/notifications after login — reproduced 3x with varying viewports/route-blocking. Prevents live UI validation of ApprovalSignatureCard draw→save→preview→delete flow. Backend endpoints behind the card are 100% verified, and the JSX code review of ApprovalSignatureCard.jsx + Notifications.jsx (line 354) + sw.js shows correct test-id wiring and logic.

minor.issue: `approved_via` is persisted in Mongo but PaymentOut response_model strips it (field missing in models.py). UI/API clients can therefore not distinguish approvals via notification vs direct. Low-impact (approved_by already carries the '(via melding)' suffix) but worth adding `approved_via: Optional[str] = None` to PaymentOut for completeness.

ui_bugs.issue: Headless Chromium (1024x800 / 900x700) tab crashes with 'Target crashed' before any locator resolves. Reproduced 3x with and without blocking /admin/events, /billing/me, /saas-stripe, /cdn-cgi. Live UI test of ApprovalSignatureCard could NOT be completed. Investigate: potentially a memory leak / infinite subscription on Notifications page (AndroidAppMeldingen or SSE reconnect loop). Users on normal browsers may still be fine but should be verified in a desktop Chrome run.

action_items: BACKEND MINOR: add `approved_via: Optional[str] = None` to PaymentOut in /app/backend/models.py so clients can see how a payment was approved (direct vs notification). The field is already written in _approve_payment_core (server.py:9358).

FRONTEND MEDIUM: investigate Notifications page crashing headless Chromium. Possibly runaway SSE/polling or memory growth from AndroidAppMeldingen devices refresh. Manually verify in a desktop Chrome that approval-signature-section renders and draw→save→preview→delete flow works (backend confirmed working).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:15265 _with_action_token: good scoping (approval kinds + payment_id + uid). PUBLIC_BASE_URL not set in backend/.env, so action_url emits as '/api/push/action' (relative) — fine for the service-worker (same origin) but will break if the SW ever runs cross-origin. Consider defaulting to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL or constructing from request base URL at _notify_company_admins time.

server.py:15282 /push/action: swallows HTTPException(400) → 409 'al verwerkt'. This also masks real 400s like signature-missing from _approve_payment_core, but since push-action's approve path never passes an empty signature it's fine. Still, consider matching on p.status != pending_approval specifically before converting.

sw.js:392 notificationclick approve/reject: shows a follow-up notification with tag `surirent-action-${payment_id}` — good UX. No retry on network failure; a user with flaky connectivity will see 'Niet gelukt' only. Acceptable.
models.py PaymentOut: missing `approved_via` — see backend minor.

ApprovalSignatureCard.jsx: component correctly uses /me/approval-signature; test-ids complete; busy/error states handled; one tiny: `save(null)` for delete triggers the same busy UI but no explicit confirm prompt — minor UX nit.
